stem: A long-term-care pharmacy receives a faxed methylphenidate Schedule II prescription for an LTCF resident. The pharmacist hesitates because methylphenidate is not a narcotic. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The LTCF fax-as-original exception can apply even though methylphenidate is nonnarcotic.
Only Schedule II narcotics can ever use an LTCF fax as original.
Methylphenidate becomes Schedule III in an LTCF.
The fax may be used only if the prescription has five refills.
LTCF status affects only inventory counting, never prescription transmission.

explanation.core_reasoning: Methylphenidate can use the LTCF C-II fax-as-original exception because that setting exception is not limited to narcotics.

choice_analysis.A: The LTCF exception is not narcotic-limited.
choice_analysis.B: That adds a restriction not in the LTCF provision.
choice_analysis.E: It is material to the fax rule.

related_facts: Hospice fax treatment has a different narcotic condition.
explanation.mpje_trap: Applying the hospice narcotic requirement to LTCF prescriptions.

reasoning_steps: Avoid importing the hospice narcotic limitation
